scope: Single-speed gears, driver view, mouse release, high-speed camera presentation, L80 curb launch

implementation.gears: Single-speed EV forward gear is displayed as D. Requests for 2–5 explicitly explain that no additional forward gears exist. Manual training gears remain available.
implementation.eyes: Native L80 eye raised 0.18 m; Seal08/manual eye raised 0.15 m. Runtime calibration, not measured OEM seat data. Native pitch -1 degree; user adjustment offsets preserved.
implementation.cabin: Ten opaque interior triangles close floor/side/firewall/rear seams. Authored windows and body stay intact. Runtime totals: Seal08 7862 triangles, L80 7874.
implementation.input: Cockpit canvas double-click resets head look. Steering requires both an active right press and the right button bit; mouse/pointer release, cancellation, blur, lost lock and late lock completion release input. Pointer lock alone no longer suppresses auto-centering.
implementation.camera: Exact vehicle translation is added to external camera and target before damping relative changes. View changes and teleports snap to the correct pose. Unneeded glass-material recompilation removed.
implementation.speed: Smooth 70–170 km/h strength ramp, at most 7 degrees extra FOV and a three-colour-tap radial edge effect. Depth rejects near-cabin taps; central view and separately rendered mirrors/HUD stay sharp. Render target allocated only once the effect becomes visible.
implementation.drive: Removed the L80 electric motor's inherited combustion-SUV 0.70 low-rpm torque factor; low-speed factor is now 1.00 with a falling high-speed curve. This is simulator calibration, not a claim of an OEM torque map. W remains 15%, Shift+W 30%. Curb work/contact resistance is retained.

newChecks: Lost-button/late-lock input guards and single-speed gear rejection
100 km/h camera-relative distance invariant under alternating frame durations at 15/30/60/120 fps
Actual GLB steering-rim clearance and nine floor-seam occlusion rays per car
Combined drivetrain and actual GLB tyre/curb solver: 18 runs across two cars, three starting poses and 30/60/120 fps; exactly one wheel starts on the curb in the single-wheel fixture
Existing left/right body-roll, actual tyre vertex penetration, coast energy loss and weak-force blockage checks still pass

browser.method: Full reload, normal menus, keyboard driving and visible T-panel test points; no hidden state injection
browser.l80Gear: Observed D label and explicit refusal message for attempting the next forward gear
browser.l80Curb: Starting at (734.45,667.14), Shift+W for 3 seconds moved to about (740,745); 14 km/h observed while braking after the run. Four contact gaps 0.00 u; both raised-side supports 2.60 u.
browser.cockpit: Both vehicles visually checked facing forward and turning head downward/right; opaque footwell and door interior, no road visible through those panels. Drag then double-click returned to the forward view.
browser.highSpeed: L80 cockpit reached approximately 97 km/h; near-follow view approximately 90 km/h. Last near-follow readout mean/p95 frame interval 17.5/28.6 ms, speed change 0.002 game units. No console errors reported.
browser.mouse: Right click/release followed by left look drag left the steering readout at zero. The browser inspection API does not expose pointerLockElement, so a direct DOM lock assertion was discarded.
browser.finalState: Game remains running at http://127.0.0.1:3000/, Seal08 cockpit, forward view, stationary with parking brake.

limits: The exact physical screen-edge drag sequence could not be replayed with the available right-drag UI API; release guards, subsequent gestures and regression checks were verified instead.
Starting with a wheel already on top of the curb is tested; this does not imply that light throttle must climb every steep vertical edge or sidewall contact.
Performance and the added edge effect were checked in the local desktop browser, not across all devices, resolutions or every vehicle.
